findings.reason: if the claim is false, the removed answer half (record_response writing the committed record when one exists, and the answer done-when) is still required, and the node's write scope and carried keys are inconsistent with the Why as written.
findings.text: §10's Why asserts "Plan-review answers are not affected: read_plan_review picks the newest candidate by modification time, so an answer written to staging after promotion stays visible", but no answer-enforcing reader is on that path: the dispatch gate calls read_plan_review(project, plan, plan=resource.path) at reckon/crew/routing.py:2810, the answer verb calls it with plan= at reckon/cli.py:2855, and MCP calls it with plan= at reckon/mcp.py:4426. With plan= set, read_plan_review returns through review_coverage (plan_review.py:990-1008), which is built from list_plan_reviews (plan_review.py:817), and list_plan_reviews reads the committed tree first and skips a staging record whose review_run_id matches one it already collected (plan_review.py:1117-1136, _plan_review_identity at :1046). record_response writes only staging, through store_plan_review -> _target_path, which never returns a committed path (plan_review.py:505-567, 1339-1351), so an answer to a promoted plan review lands in staging carrying the committed record's review_run_id and is shadowed: the gate reads the committed copy and keeps refusing, and the answer verb even reports success because cli.py:2885 checks unanswered_findings on the locally re-read staging file. The section as narrowed drops the plan-review half of the deliverable while claiming it needs no work — yet the Deliverable still lists plan_review.py as a write path and still carries "responses" and "response_events" (keys only plan reviews carry; run reviews carry dimension_dispositions), contradicting the Why's own claim.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — review.stored_record (reckon/crew/review.py:2188), review.record_dimension_disposition (review.py:2800), read_plan_review (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:964) and _commit_state_write (reckon/ledger.py:1693) all resolve; the imas-codex run id is an external trace.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — both done-when clauses carry a falsifier: the promotion case "fails when promotion stops carrying dispositions", and the post-promotion case "fails when the commit is removed".
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the section writes no evidence to a scratchpad or node-local path; its evidence is the tests the done-when names.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags reach the section's symbols or prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §10's Why declares plan-review answers unaffected because read_plan_review selects the newest candidate by mtime, but every reader that enforces an answer calls read_plan_review with plan=..., taking the review_coverage/list_plan_reviews path where the committed copy shadows the staging answer.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — one node, one invariant (a disposition survives promotion on either side of it), with two changes that serve that single verdict.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §10 declares no relationships and names three write paths (reckon/crew/review.py, plan_review.py, promotion.py), and its only overlap is §9's plan_review.py claim, which the dispatch scope check refuses to run concurrently, so no plan-level edge is required.
